newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police raid homes of N.League supporters.
newsitem.headline: Italian police raid homes of N.League supporters.

text.p: Italian police said they raided homes of supporters of the separatist Northern League on Thursday in connection with a probe into the alleged formation of a military-type organisation.

Verona public prosecutor Guido Papalia ordered 17 raids, mainly in the Lombardy and Veneto regions, on officials of the League's security service, the so-called national guard of Padania, formerly called the Greenshirts.

League sources said police had seized shirts, badges, flags and manifestos plus 20 photocopies of the text of "Va Pensiero", the aria from Verdi's opera Nabucco which the League has adopted as its "hymn".
It was the second swoop in two months on the League.
League leader Umberto Bossi vowed to press on with the formation of a militia for its self-styled state of Padania after a raid on its Milan headquarters in September.
Police were accused of heavy-handed tactics during that raid when scuffles broke out as they forced their way in.
League parliamentarian Roberto Maroni, interior minister in Silvio Berlusconi's short-lived government in 1994, was punched and needed hospital treatment.

The Milan raid was part of an inquiry into the League and its security squad for alleged anti-constitutional activity following Bossi's declaration of "independence" for his would-be republic in northern Italy in September.

The League, condemning police action as "fascist tactics", has said the incidents were likely to speed up recruitment of a Padanian national guard, announced by Bossi as one of the first planned acts of his new state.
The Northern League won an unexpected 10.7 percent in Italy's general elections in April but surveys show most northerners firmly oppose secession.
